title: Senior Research Manager - Animal Welfare
description:
About the role

Rethink Priorities' Animal Welfare Department produces research and strategic advice to help organizations make well-informed decisions for animals. The Department is splitting into three teams. The AI and Animals Team helps organisations navigate an AI-transforming world. The Frontiers Team advances the field of animal welfare, focusing on neglected animals (such as shrimp) and emerging topics (such as breeding for welfare). And a new Animal Welfare Strategy Team, described below.

The Animal Welfare Strategy Team (working name) will focus on supporting and accelerating funders and organizations toward achieving their core goals of accelerating the end of low-welfare farming and reducing the suffering of animals on farms, with a focus on terrestrial vertebrates. This will involve a mix of consulting work, in-house research, and other activities.
  • Recent consulting work has included economic analysis of egg prices for a policy advocacy organization, prioritization of welfare-tech ideas for a venture studio, and research on alternative-protein regulation to guide a large grantmaker with a $10m+ portfolio. RP is independent: clients get the answers that the evidence supports, whether or not they are the ones they hoped for.
  • In-house research might involve building data tools and resources to map where animals are suffering on farms, or strategic analysis to guide stakeholders' decisions.
  • The team will also run the annual Animal Advocacy Strategy Forum, which brings together leaders from across the animal welfare landscape. Going forward, it may build capacity for other actions to enable the success for existing and new projects, such as regranting or talent programs.
The department seeks to hire a Senior Research Manager to lead this new Animal Welfare Strategy Team. This is a leadership role in a Department that is growing and being restructured. You will need to work with the Director to set a strategy for this team covering how the team prioritizes projects, and how the team measures and maximizes impact for the animals. We are looking for someone excited to build these structures. You will also work on hiring, managing incoming consulting projects, designing research processes, and managing staff. We want to create a team with a mix of cross-cutting skills, such as economics, policy, animal welfare ecosystem knowledge, stakeholder management, M&E, and animal science. We have 1–2 economist staff ready to join this team.

This role will report to Sam Hilton, Acting Director of the Animal Welfare Department.
Ideal start date: Monday 4th January 2027

Key Responsibilities

You are responsible for leading the team's areas of work. This includes:
  • Manage consulting intake. Decide which requests from funders, advocacy organizations, and entrepreneurs RP takes on, reshapes, or declines.
  • Identify opportunities and act on them. Bring forward ideas with outsized upside, research or otherwise. For research, set an agenda of priority projects. For other interventions, such as regranting or talent programs, decide whether RP should run them and launch what clears the bar.
  • Oversee the Animal Advocacy Strategy Forum. Ensure your team: sets the agenda, decides who is in the room, and turns the movement's annual leaders' gathering into decisions and impact.
Your day-to-day responsibilities will include:
  • Set strategy. Decide how this team prioritizes, how it measures impact and what work it takes on. There is no project prioritization process, impact framework or intake system yet – you will build them alongside the Director.
  • Hire. Decide which skills the team needs next: policy, M&E, animal science, movement experience. Run the rounds, supported by RP's in-house recruitment specialist.
  • Manage the team. Lead economists and specialists with deeper expertise than yours in their own fields. Set the quality bar. Put in place research processes, review standards and project tracking.
  • Deliver research that gets used. Scope clients' decisions, manage staff to deliver on deadline, and follow up on whether clients acted on the findings.
  • Represent RP. Build the networks and relationships that generate new projects. Attend conferences where you are able to travel.
  • Fundraise. With the Development Team's support, raise additional funds as the team grows.

What We Are Looking For

Essential criteria

  • Impact first. Driven to have as much impact for animals as possible. Committed to integrity in research, to following the evidence, and to being transparent about what it shows.
  • Decision-oriented research experience. Experience conducting or overseeing research aimed at informing or influencing a specific stakeholder's decision.
  • Good judgment. Demonstrated judgment in prioritization and decision-making under uncertainty.
  • Management experience. Experience managing or mentoring others, including people with deeper expertise than yours, or clear readiness to step into a people-management role.
  • Strategy and process design. Experience of, or clear ability to set a team's strategy and build processes to deliver it where none existed.
  • Research review skills. Ability to interrogate both qualitative and quantitative analysis you did not produce, and to "think at the margin" about cost-effectiveness.
  • Communication skills. Excellent reasoning transparency: ability to show the assumptions and evidence behind your conclusions. Strong ability to synthesize complex information and communicate strategic insight in writing and in person.
  • Delivery. Track record of getting projects finished, on deadline, involving other people. Works well and makes autonomous decisions in a remote, asynchronous, international environment.

Desirable criteria

  • Consulting experience. Consulting or other client-facing analytical work: identifying the decision a client is actually facing, shaping or declining work accordingly, and building relationships with clients and fundraising leads.
  • Experience of the animal organizational landscape. Professional or voluntary experience of animal advocacy. A working knowledge of the organizational landscape, funders, and strategic debates.
  • In-depth expertise in a relevant area. Such as economics, policy and regulation, M&E, or animal science.
  • Events and convening experience. Running convenings or facilitating events that bring together groups with differing interests.
  • Talent development experience. Running talent programs or fellowships.
  • Grantmaking experience. Distributing funds and evaluating organizations for funding.
We expect that even highly qualified applicants will not meet all of these criteria. We encourage you to apply even if you do not have some of these skills, knowledge and experiences.

What We Offer

Compensation

  • We offer an annual salary within the following ranges for a full-time position, prorated for part-time work:
    • $98,500 - $125,000 USD pre-tax
    • £76,590 - £97,176 GBP pre-tax
    • €89,459 - €113,527 EUR pre-tax
  • Compensation is not restricted to the currencies listed above.
  • The exact salary will be based on the candidate’s title level, and calculated using RP’s salary algorithm. Towards the upper end we would expect a track record of leading a research team to drive impact. Towards the lower end we would expect strong research judgment with a shorter management record, or management experience but weaker research skills. You do not need to say which end you think you fit; we assess this from your application.
  • To ensure fairness across the entire organization, RP does not negotiate salaries.

Other Benefits

  • Opportunity to contribute to a fast-growing, high-impact organization — our research is used by key decision-makers who influence the distribution of hundreds of millions of charitable dollars.
  • Remote-first environment, including flexible work hours and schedule. Virtual co-working spaces, including a private Rethink Priorities Focusmate group
  • Comprehensive global benefits program, including statutory benefits as required by local law, and supplemental benefits specific to each country (varies by location)
  • Generous paid time off (PTO) and unpaid leave, including:
    • Unlimited vacation with a minimum number of required statutory days off
    • "Mandated" 3 weeks total mid- and end-year organization-wide breaks
    • Unlimited (within reason) personal and sick paid and unpaid leave
    • Parental leave — at least 4 - 9 months of a combination of paid and unpaid leave, available prior to and/or during the first 2 years after a child's birth or adoption
    • Other paid and unpaid leave (e.g., bereavement)
  • Technology stipend of $2,000 USD equivalent every 3 years for work and office equipment and an AI tools budget of $40 USD equivalent monthly
  • Professional Development Budget of $4000 USD per year. Learning opportunities, including workshops/training sessions and up to 10% of work time dedicated to professional and personal development
  • Paid work trips, including one annual all-staff Mega Team Retreat and relevant conferences
  • A caring team that values respectful work relations and a healthy work-life balance.
  • Low administrative bureaucracy.
  • We don’t provide snacks, but we could mail you a box of Oreos if you want!

Apply here

Application deadline Mon 19th October, end of day (anywhere on earth). Please click the link on the sidebar / at the foot of this page to apply.

Additional Information

Role-Specific

  • Work Environment and Visa Sponsorship: This role is fully remote and we are able to legally hire in many countries. In certain cases, we may be able to provide visa sponsorship to the US or UK and help candidates relocate. If you have questions about whether we can hire or provide visa sponsorship in another country and if this will influence your decision about applying, please contact before submitting your application.
  • Time Zones and Working Hours: While we welcome applicants from all time zones, you will need to have some availability for meetings between 3pm and 5pm UK time on most weekdays, when our Europe-based and US Central time based colleagues overlap. Depending on where you are, this may mean early morning or evening calls.
  • Full and Part Time Position: This role is open to full-time and part-time candidates who are available to work at least 24 hours per week. Candidates able to work at least 30 hours a week will be preferred.
  • Travel: Travel is not an essential requirement for this position. Travel is not mandatory, but encouraged. A majority of our staff travel a few times pe

title: Key Stage 2 Class Teacher
location: Bury St. Edmunds, East of England, GB
description:
Anglian Learning - Transforming Education Together

Key Stage 2 Class Teacher

Salary: Teacher Main/Upper Pay Scale, M1 (£32,916) - U3 (£51,048) FTE, plus TLR 2.1 (£3,527) per annum if applicable, subject to the September 2026 pay award.

Contract Type: Full time , Permanent

Expected Start Date: January 2027, subject to satisfactory pre-employment checks.

Interview Date: Thursday, 15ᵗʰ October 2026

How to Apply: Please apply via our recruitment portal. We are unable to accept CVs.

*************************************************************************

Please note we reserve the right to interview prior to the advertised closing date. Therefore, we encourage interested applicants to apply as soon as possible.

Role overview:

Anglian Learning is pleased to share with you an exciting opportunity for an enthusiastic and experienced Key Stage 2 Class Teacher to join the team at The Pines Primary School.

Alongside responsibility for the academic achievement and pastoral care of your class, you will play an important role in supporting high-quality teaching and learning across the school.

An enhanced opportunity is also available for candidates interested in taking on an additional leadership responsibility. This would attract a Teaching and Learning Responsibility (TLR) payment. Working closely with the Headteacher, the successful candidate taking on this additional responsibility will contribute to curriculum and assessment development, support and influence colleagues’ practice, monitor standards and pupil outcomes, and contribute to whole-school improvement.

When applying, please state whether you wish to be considered for the standard teaching role or the teaching role with the additional leadership responsibility.

The successful candidate will:

  • hold Qualified Teacher Status (QTS)
  • have proven successful teaching experience and a strong understanding of effective teaching, learning and assessment
  • have high expectations for all pupils and a commitment to securing strong outcomes
  • be able to support and influence colleagues through modelling, coaching and professional dialogue
  • have strong organisational, communication and interpersonal skills
  • be committed to safeguarding, inclusion and the wider life of the school

As an employee of Anglian Learning, you would benefit from access to a range of employee benefits and Trust-wide initiatives. For an overview of the benefits on offer please refer to the Recruitment Information Pack.

*Regrettably we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Applicants must either have the legal right to work in the UK at the time of application or be in the process of obtaining this, as proof of right to work will be required during the recruitment process.

If working for an organisation that strives to have a long-lasting positive impact on its pupils and local community sounds appealing then we want to hear from you!

For further information about the role requirements, our Trust and school, please see the attached documentation.

**************************************************************************

We value diversity and welcome applications from all, irrespective of gender, marital status, disability, race, age or sexual orientation. As a Disability Confident Employer we are committed to working with applicants and existing staff to explore ways in which we can remove barriers to support everyone to fulfil their potential. If you would benefit from adjustments in order to make the recruitment process more accessible for you, please get in contact to discuss options.

Anglian Learning is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of young people and vulnerable adults. We expect all staff to share this commitment and undergo appropriate checks. Therefore, all posts within the Trust are subject to robust pre-employment checks including but not limited to checks carried out by the Disclosure and Barring Service and an online presence check prior to interview.

This role is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act. Our policies for Ex-Offenders, GDPR, Safeguarding and Recruitment can be found on our website: www.anglianlearning.org

title: Level 1 Teaching Assistant
description:
Job Title: Teaching Assistant – Level 1 (SEN) 

Actual Annual Salary: £4,844 - £5,280 based on hours and weeks worked 

Full Time Equivalent Salary: £26,798 - £29,208 (CLF Grade B) based on full time hours, all year round.  

Contract Type:  Fixed Term Contract until 31 August 2027 

Hours of work: 8 hours per week, Term Time Only (Monday to Thursday) 

 

Potential Start Date: 23 November 2026 – pending completion of pre-employment checks  

Are you ready to take an a supportive role within a classroom environment: 

We are looking for a passionate and inspiring Teaching Assistant - Level 1 to join our supportive and talented team at Redstart Primary. We are part of a diverse multi-academy trust, looking for professional and ambitious people, with a passion for transforming our pupils’ learning.  

The Redstart Primary School is a two-form entry primary academy, located in Chard, Somerset, taking children from Nursery to Year 6. 

We aim to develop a love of learning in our children to last through their lives. We believe passionately in our children having the highest aspirations and are committed to providing a broad and balanced curriculum with exciting opportunities including access to a rich programme of after school activities. We want to enable all our children to realise their full potential, their talents and their interests in all areas.  

We are looking for a Teaching Assistant - Level 1, to assist in the educational, personal, and social development of designated students under the direction and guidance of relevant colleagues (e.g. the Principal, SENCo and Assistant Principal). Support students by adopting relevant strategies and techniques to enable them to access the curriculum, engage with their learning and achieve their full potential. Takes responsibility for implementing planned learning activities/ teaching programmes as agreed with the teacher, adjusting activities according to students’ responses as appropriate. Deliver measurable impact on student attainment as well as social and emotional well-being. Works collaboratively with relevant colleagues to fulfil the requirements of the role.  

About you:    

You will:  

• Be committed to being part of a high performing school that has high expectations.   

• Continuously be committed to improving the life chances of pupils.   

• Always be committed to own self development and resilient to the challenges of working in a single form entry school.   

• Be committed to seeing feedback as a gift and strive to be better every day.   

• Stay committed to the wider success of the school and community.  

• Have experience of, or willingness to embrace working in a single form entry school is essential.  

• Have an understanding of classroom roles and responsibilities and how a teaching assistant supports students in their learning.  

• Be able to engage students and manage behaviour on a one to one or small group basis.  

• Be committed to undertake relevant qualifications, e.g. Relevant nvq level 2/ 3 in supporting teaching and learning or equivalent, first aid qualification, to ensure ongoing professional development.  

• Be able to engage students and manage behaviour on a one to one or small group basis.  

• Have strong interpersonal skills, in particular with the ability to demonstrate empathy and active listening.  

• Have good planning and organisational skills, specifically with regard to learning activities and support materials.  

• Be someone with a keen interest in working with children and commitment to inclusion and acceptance of all.  

Applicants are advised to refer to the full requirements of the role in the attached job description and person specification, prior to submitting an application.    

About Restart Primary Academy: 

Redstart Primary School is a two-form entry primary academy, located in Chard, Somerset, taking children from Nursery to Year 6.  

We aim to develop a love of learning in our children to last through their lives. We believe passionately in our children having the highest aspirations and are committed to providing a broad and balanced curriculum with exciting opportunities including access to a rich programme of after school activities. We want to enable all our children to realise their full potential, their talents and their interests in all areas.   

Why CLF? 

We are a diverse and inclusive community of 37 academies across five cluster regions in the South West that is committed to excellence and making a positive impact. Our people bring unique perspectives, but we’re all driven by a shared moral purpose and a passion for making a positive impact, whether in a teaching, leadership or support role. We’re proud to foster a culture where everyone can thrive, feel valued, and make a meaningful difference to the lives of others. 

We are an equal opportunity employer and proud to serve a diverse student population and our communities. We strongly believe that representation matters and so encourage applications from underrepresented and global majority groups including ethnicity, gender, transgender, age, disability, sexual orientation or religion. 

We aim to remove any barriers to employment, ensuring everyone can compete on equal terms. Job share, part-time and flexible working opportunities will be considered. 

What we can offer you:  

  • Access to a generous pension through the Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS).  
  • Generous annual leave.  
  • A comprehensive induction and ongoing commitment to wellbeing and career progression, through a range of training, apprenticeships and in-role/wider-trust development opportunities.  
  • Well-being support through an Employee Assistance Programme.  
  • Health benefits, including wellness sessions, gym discounts, and flu jabs.  
  • A range of generous family leave options, including above industry average occupational maternity pay.  
  • Additional benefits like cycle to work scheme, on-site parking plus many more! 

Recruitment timeline: 

Closing Date: 12 October 2026 @11.59pm 

Short-listing: 13 October 2026 

Interviews: 19 October 2026 

We welcome visits from potential candidates. If you would like to arrange a school visit prior to the closing date, please contact the academy/site directly to arrange a suitable appointment. 

As part of our commitment to Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE), we do not accept CVs – a full education and employment history must be provided through our application form. 

This role may be eligible for Skilled Worker visa sponsorship, subject to the candidate meeting the applicable Home Office eligibility and salary requirements. Full-time and 0.8 FTE positions will generally meet the required salary threshold; for other part-time working arrangements, eligibility will depend on the salary applicable to the role and the candidate's working pattern. 

We reserve the right to close this vacancy early, should we receive a high level of interest in the role. Therefore, candidates are advised to apply at their earliest convenience to avoid missing out.    

As a Disability Confident Committed Employer, we are dedicated to equity and inclusion and commit to interviewing applicants with a disability who meet the essential criteria. We aim to provide an inclusive and accessible recruitment process, and support employees throughout their employment. If you have a disability, are neurodivergent, or require any adjustments to support you through the application or interview process please let us know how we can assist.

title: Afterschool Club Playworker - Fixed Term Contract
description:
Job Title: Afterschool Playworker 

Actual Annual Salary: £8,063 - £8,200 Based on working hours and weeks. 

Full Time Equivalent Salary: £25,949 - £26,392 (CLF Grade Aii) Based on 37 hours per week, all year round.  

Contract: Fixed Term Contract until October 2027 or the return of the current postholder (maternity cover)  

Hours: 13.75 per week (Monday - Friday 3:00pm – 5:45pm)  

Provisional Start Date: As soon as possible - pending completion of pre employment checks

We are looking for an enthusiastic Playworker to join our after-school provision, supporting children through play, learning and enrichment activities at the end of the school day.  

We are seeking a dedicated and enthusiastic Playworker to join our team, providing a safe and engaging environment for children. The ideal candidate will have a passion for working with young children, demonstrating strong leadership skills and the ability to communicate effectively with both children and parents. This role is essential in supporting children's development through play and structured activities within a primary setting.  

Duties  

  • Support the day-to-day running of the after-school provision, ensuring a safe, stimulating and inclusive environment for all children.  
  • Communicate effectively with children, encouraging their participation in play and learning activities.  
  • Supervise children during playtime, ensuring their safety and well-being at all times.  
  • Plan and implement engaging activities that promote physical, social, and emotional development.  
  • Foster positive relationships with children, parents, and colleagues to create a supportive community.  
  • Maintain cleanliness and organisation of the play area, ensuring all equipment is safe and suitable for use.  
  • Collaborate with other staff members to support the overall objectives of the after-school club.  

About you:  

You will:  

  • have an understanding of the varied needs of children and families.  
  • have an appropriate First Aid qualification or willingness to undertake training.  
  • have strong interpersonal skills, in particular demonstrates empathy and active listening.  
  • be able to deal with inappropriate behaviour in a calm and non-judgemental way, following academy guidance.  
  • be patient, calm and able to work under pressure.  

Applicants are advised to refer to the full requirements of the role in the attached job description and person specification, prior to submitting an application.

Wallscourt Farm Academy is two-form entry primary school located in Stoke Gifford, on the outskirts of Bristol and South Gloucestershire.   

At Wallscourt Farm , we foster ambitious young people who are culturally aware and who contribute to society and the lives of others. We value tolerance, understanding, mutual respect, unique individuality and celebrate the unity that this makes as we come together as one learning community. These principles underpin everything that happens within and around the school and bind us as individuals within diverse communities that come together with one shared goal – to contribute positively to our own lives and to the lives of others.   

We hold high expectations for our learners and have crafted a curriculum that is progressive, well-sequenced, coherent, and inspiring.   

Wallscourt Farm also has a positive, passionate and ambitious staff team. We value the part that each and every staff member plays in achieving our vision. We work hard to make people feel welcome and included and have created our own staff culture tree cookies.  

Why work at CLF?

Over 41% of the pupils who attend Wallscourt Farm Academy are from global majority groups, so we particularly encourage applicants from those groups in order to represent the pupils we serve, as well as wider underrepresented groups including gender, transgender, age disability, sexual orientation or religion.  

We aim to remove any barriers to employment, ensuring everyone can compete on equal terms. Job share, part-time and flexible working opportunities will be considered.

  • Access to a generous pension through the Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS).

  • A comprehensive induction and ongoing commitment to wellbeing and career progression, through a range of training, apprenticeships and in-role/wider-trust development opportunities.  
  • Well-being support through an Employee Assistance Programme.

title: Administrative Assistant
description:
Job Title: Administration Assistant (Level 1)

Actual Annual Salary: £9,542 - £10,400 Based on hours and working weeks

Full Time Equivalent Salary: £26,798 - £29,208 (CLF Grade B) Based on 37 hours per week, all year round

Contract Type: Permanent, Term Time Only plus Inset Days and an additional 2 days (In line with working pattern) 

Hours of Work: Part-Time, 15 hours per week, Wednesday and Thursday (7.5 hours per day) 

Provisional Start Date: 12 October 2026 - pending the completion of pre-employment checks 

An opportunity to play a key role at the heart of our academy, providing a welcoming and professional front-of-house service while supporting the day-to-day administration that helps our students, staff and families thrive. 

We are looking for an Administration Assistant to join our supportive and talented team at Kingsmead Academy. Working under the direction of senior staff, you will provide general administrative and clerical support across the academy, acting as a first point of contact for parents, students, visitors and external agencies. This is a varied role that combines reception responsibilities, pupil welfare support and essential administrative duties that contribute to the smooth running of the academy. 

As the first point of contact for the academy, you will provide a professional and welcoming service to students, parents, visitors and external agencies, ensuring enquiries are handled efficiently and positively. You will play an important role in supporting student welfare and day-to-day academy operations, maintaining accurate records, managing communications and helping to ensure information is processed effectively and confidentially. Working as part of the wider administration team, you will contribute to the smooth running of the academy by providing high-quality administrative support, promoting excellent customer service and upholding the academy's safeguarding responsibilities. First aid training will be provided to enable you to support students when required. 

About You 

You will have: 

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build positive relationships with students, families, staff and visitors whilst providing a professional and welcoming service. 
  • Strong organisational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to maintain accurate records, manage competing priorities and meet deadlines in a busy school environment. 
  • Good IT skills, including experience of Microsoft Office applications, email systems and administrative databases, together with the ability to learn new systems quickly. 
  • The ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team, using initiative and sound judgement whilst maintaining confidentiality at all times. 
  • A caring, patient and professional approach, with a genuine commitment to supporting the welfare, safety and success of children and young people. 
  • GCSE English and Maths (Grade 4/C or above, or equivalent qualifications) and a willingness to undertake relevant training where required. 

This is an excellent opportunity for a committed, enthusiastic and hardworking individual who takes pride in delivering high-quality administrative support and contributing positively to academy life. If you thrive in a busy environment, enjoy working with people and are passionate about supporting young people to succeed, we would love to hear from you. 

Applicants are advised to refer to the full requirements of the role in the attached job description and person specification, prior to submitting an application. 

About Kingsmead Academy: 

Kingsmead School is a rural mixed ability Academy with a fully comprehensive intake situated near the Devon/Somerset border, close to the Brendon Hills and Exmoor. It is a magnificent area in which to live and work. Not only is there the tranquillity and beauty of the countryside but there is the rapidly growing county town of Taunton nearby and easy access (20 minutes) to the M5 for connections to the rest of the country. 

The school lies in the small town of Wiveliscombe. It caters for the age range 11-16 and has 884 students and just over 100 staff. Our latest Ofsted Report, in June 2022, gave an overall judgement that Kingsmead “requires improvement”. Mr J Eddy, Headteacher, joined Kingsmead in January 2023. He is determined to improve education at Kingsmead for our superb body of students. 

The core values of Kingsmead are Care, Aspiration, Respect and Determination which drive our strong positive ethos and offering amenities for the whole school community. We have high expectations and expect staff to support our caring, student-centred ethos to set high standards for our students. We hope staff will contribute to and lead some of the wide range of extra-curricular opportunities we offer. 

Why work at CLF? 

We are a diverse and inclusive community of 37 academies across five cluster regions in the South West that is committed to excellence and making a positive impact. Our people bring unique perspectives, but we’re all driven by a shared moral purpose and a passion for making a positive impact, whether in a teaching, leadership or support role. We’re proud to foster a culture where everyone can thrive, feel valued, and make a meaningful difference to the lives of others. 

We are an equal opportunity employer and proud to serve a diverse student population and our communities. We strongly believe that representation matters and so encourage applications from underrepresented and global majority groups including ethnicity, gender, transgender, age, disability, sexual orientation or religion. 

We aim to remove any barriers to employment, ensuring everyone can compete on equal terms. Job share, part-time and flexible working opportunities will be considered. 

What we can offer you: 

  • Access to a generous pension through the Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS). 
  • Generous annual leave. 
  • A comprehensive induction and ongoing commitment to wellbeing and career progression, through a range of training, apprenticeships and in-role/wider-trust development opportunities. 
  • Well-being support through an Employee Assistance Programme. 
  • Health benefits, including wellness sessions, gym discounts, and flu jabs. 
  • A range of generous family leave options, including above industry average occupational maternity pay. 
  • Additional benefits like cycle to work scheme, on-site parking plus many more! 

Recruitment timeline: 

Closing Date: 14 October 2026 @11.59pm 

Shortlisting: 15 October 2026 

Interviews: Week commencing 02 November 2026 

We welcome visits from potential candidates. If you would like to arrange a school visit prior to the closing date, please contact the academy/site directly to arrange a suitable appointment. 

As part of our commitment to Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE), we do not accept CVs – a full education and employment history must be provided through our application form.

title: Exams Invigilator
description:
Job Title: Exam Invigilators 

Hourly Rate: £13.45 (Grade Aii) 

Contract Type: Casual Basis 

Potential Start: December 2026 (Subject to completion of pre-employment checks) 

An opportunity to provide flexible, casual support to the academy team during busy exam periods: 

We are looking for Exam Invigilators to join our supportive and talented exam team at Kingsmead Academy. We are a diverse multi-academy trust, looking for professional and ambitious people, with a passion for transforming our students’ learning. Our Academies need exam invigilators, readers and scribers to assist with scheduled exams across the Federation. As this is a casual position you will work when available and will be called upon when required to support the Academy during exam season. 

This position requires flexibility as there are various exams held throughout the academic year, these usually fall within November, January and March. The Summer exams are held in May and June.  There are also mock exams for Years 9, 10 and 11 at different times throughout the year.  The working hours for this role can vary as exam environments have to be set up before the beginning of the school day and on occasions can sometimes continue after the school day has finished. 

About you: 

You will have: 

  • practical experience of understanding and following processes and procedure. 
  • excellent interpersonal, good organisational and time management skills. 
  • the ability to keep calm under pressure or during unexpected circumstances. 
  • have a caring and understanding attitude, sensitive and responsive to the needs of our students. 
  • the capabilities to work as part of a team but also under own initiative.  

Applicants are advised to refer to the full requirements of the role in the attached job description and person specification, prior to submitting an application.  

About Kingsmead Academy:  

Kingsmead School is a rural mixed ability Academy with a fully comprehensive intake situated near the Devon/Somerset border, close to the Brendon Hills and Exmoor. It is a magnificent area in which to live and work. Not only is there the tranquillity and beauty of the countryside but there is the rapidly growing county town of Taunton nearby and easy access (20 minutes) to the M5 for connections to the rest of the country.  

The school lies in the small town of Wiveliscombe. It caters for the age range 11-16 and has 884 students and just over 100 staff. Our latest Ofsted Report, in June 2022, gave an overall judgement that Kingsmead “requires improvement”. Mr J Eddy, Headteacher, joined Kingsmead in January 2023. He is determined to improve education at Kingsmead for our superb body of students.  

The core values of Kingsmead are Care, Aspiration, Respect and Determination which drive our strong positive ethos and offering amenities for the whole school community. We have high expectations and expect staff to support our caring, student-centred ethos to set high standards for our students. We hope staff will contribute to and lead some of the wide range of extra-curricular opportunities we offer.  

Why work at CLF?  

We are a diverse and inclusive community of 37 academies across five cluster regions in the South West that is committed to excellence and making a positive impact. Our people bring unique perspectives, but we’re all driven by a shared moral purpose and a passion for making a positive impact, whether in a teaching, leadership or support role. We’re proud to foster a culture where everyone can thrive, feel valued, and make a meaningful difference to the lives of others.  

We are an equal opportunity employer and proud to serve a diverse student population and our communities. We strongly believe that representation matters and so encourage applications from underrepresented and global majority groups including ethnicity, gender, transgender, age, disability, sexual orientation or religion.  

We aim to remove any barriers to employment, ensuring everyone can compete on equal terms. Job share, part-time and flexible working opportunities will be considered. 

What we can offer you: 

  • Access to a generous pension through the Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS). 
  • Generous annual leave. 
  • A comprehensive induction and ongoing commitment to wellbeing and career progression, through a range of training, apprenticeships and in-role/wider-trust development opportunities. 
  • Well-being support through an Employee Assistance Programme. 
  • Health benefits, including wellness sessions, gym discounts, and flu jabs. 
  • A range of generous family leave options, including above industry average occupational maternity pay. 
  • Additional benefits like cycle to work scheme, on-site parking plus many more! 

Recruitment timeline: 

Closing Date: 19 October 2026 @11.59pm 

Shortlisting Date: 20/21 October 2026 

Interviews: Week commencing 02 November 2026 

We welcome visits from potential candidates. If you would like to arrange a school visit prior to the closing date, please contact the academy/site directly to arrange a suitable appointment. 

As part of our commitment to Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE), we do not accept CVs - a full education and employment history must be provided through our application form. 

Please note we are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role. 

We reserve the right to close this vacancy early, should we receive a high level of interest in the role. Therefore, candidates are advised to apply at their earliest convenience to avoid missing out.

We aim to provide an inclusive and accessible recruitment process, and support employees throughout their employment. If you have a disability, are neurodivergent, or require any adjustments to support you through the application or interview process please let us know how we can assist.

Manor School is renowned as a beacon of excellence both within the local community and beyond; it is part of a growing and dynamic Trust (The Rise Partnership Trust).

Manor School is an outstanding special school located within the vibrant community of the London Borough of Brent. Proudly part of The Rise Partnership Trust, we cater for 220 incredible primary-aged children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND).

The school is split across three sites in Brent: Manor School, Chamberlayne Road in Kensal Rise, the Manor School Early Years Centre (MSEYC) is on Bridge Road in Neasden. And our third Site is at Canterbury Road, Kilburn. We are recruiting for a Class teacher at the Kensal Rise (Chamberlayne Rd) site at this time but would like to share that in the future, as a three site school, staff may be asked to work at any of the three sites.

Manor School is an exceptional place to work and we pride ourselves on offering an excellent Continuous Professional Development (CPD) program, generous PPA allocations, a warm and inclusive atmosphere and abundant opportunities for career advancement.

Please check out our Social Media to see what we’re all about: @manorschldn @ManorSchBrent

We are seeking an exceptional candidate who is deeply passionate about working with children with SEND. As a teacher at Manor School, you will play a pivotal role in nurturing the development and growth of our youngest learners, providing them with the support, guidance, and education they need to thrive.

We are seeking a candidate whose skills, experience, and character align with our warm, friendly, and highly ambitious culture. We value individuals who are not only passionate about working with children with SEND but also embody our school motto: “Love, Learn, Laugh.”

Please see attached Job Description and Person Specification to see what we’re looking for in the ideal candidate.

Visa Sponsorship Eligibility

Safeguarding Statement *

The Rise Partnership Trust take its’ responsibilities in relation to safeguarding and child protection very seriously. All appointments to the school are subject to Enhanced Disclosure by the Disclosure and Barring Service and comprehensive pre-employment checks.

This post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 and therefore applicants are required to declare:

All unspent convictions and conditional cautions

All spent convictions and adult cautions that are not protected (i.e. that are not filtered out) as defined by the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (Exceptions) Order 1975 (as amended in 2020).

For further information on filtering please refer to Nacro guidance and the guidance issued by the Ministry of Justice (see, in particular, the section titled ‘Exceptions Order’).

It is an offence to apply for the role if you are barred from engaging in regulated activity relevant to children. All shortlisted applicants will be required to complete self-disclosure form and return prior to interview.

At Pinterest, we’re on a mission to bring everyone the inspiration to create a life they love, and that starts with the people behind the product.

 Discover a career where you ignite innovation for millions, transform passion into growth opportunities, celebrate each other’s unique experiences and embrace the flexibility to do your best work. Creating a career you love? It’s Possible.

To get a complete picture of your experience and abilities, we’ll explore your foundational skills and how you collaborate with AI.

 Through our interview process, what matters most is that you can always explain your approach, showing us not just what you know, but how you think. You can read more about our AI interview philosophy and how we use AI in our recruiting process here .

 As a Financial Manager focused onTechnology Infrastructure, you will have financial and strategic oversight for managing and optimizing the significant investments Pinterest makes in its technology infrastructure (primarily AWS, our cloud-based computational and storage provider). This is a critical role that sits at the center of how Pinterest executes its technology and innovation strategy. You will play a key role - in partnership with technology infrastructure leadership - in governing our infrastructure investments, managing key vendor relationships (especially AWS) and ensuring we can cost effectively serve Pinners and Advertisers while also enabling future technological innovation … while also being able to allocate and track costs at the appropriate level within the company. These teams and technology service providers are the foundation of our online service as well as how our Engineering, Product and Design teams execute their work.

title: Partner Marketing Manager
description:
Headquarters: United States, Remote

 Our Mission:

 6sense's mission is to multiply what matters: growth, retention, and efficiency. We envision a future where companies, teams and people reach their full potential.

 Our People:

 People are the heart and soul of 6sense. We serve with passion and purpose. We live by our Being 6sense values of Win as One Team, Stay Curious, Do The Right Thing, Own the Outcome, and Create Belonging. Every 6sensor plays a part in deﬁning the future of our industry-leading technology. 6sense is a place where difference-makers roll up their sleeves, take risks, act with integrity, and measure success by the value we create for our customers. We want 6sense to be the best chapter of your career.

 As our Partner Marketing Manager you will be responsible for turning strategic partnerships into a measurable pipeline motion- building the co-marketing programs, and partner activation strategies that help communicate the power of 6Sense alongside our key partners. This is a builder's role for someone who wants to own a meaningful piece of how 6sense grows, and who understands that great partner marketing sits at the intersection of relationship depth and disciplined execution.

 Responsibilities :

• Joint Go-to-Market Programs
 Build and run co-marketing programs with strategic partners , from end to end: partner alignment, asset development, campaign execution, field activation, and measurement. Own the pipeline contribution from partner marketing activity and be accountable for reporting it clearly.

• Joint Events and Activations
 Own the partner presence at key industry events (including our own, BreakThrough ), co-hosted webinars, and joint field programs. Coordinate logistics , messaging, and follow-up across both sides of the partnership to make sure activations generate pipeline .

• Partner Relationships
 Serve as the primary marketing counterpart to partner marketing and alliances teams at key accounts. Build the kind of working relationships where partner counterparts are actively seeking us out. Create opportunities for 6sense to co-present at joint events, and develop the trust that makes joint programs move faster.

• Partner Marketing Metrics
 Define what success looks like for partner marketing at 6sense, working with marketing operations to build the reporting infrastructure to measure it, and communicate results to marketing leadership and BD stakeholders on a regul ar cade nce .

• Performance Measurement

• Partner-Sourced Pipeline
 Volume and velocity of pipeline generated through co-marketing programs and partner activations, tracked with clear attribution.

• Partner Marketing Engagement
 Depth of engagement from partner counterparts: co-investment in programs, co-branded content produced, joint events executed, and partner-sourced leads generated.

• Enablement Adoption
 Usage and effectiveness of partner-facing enablement materials, measured by partner sales team feedback and co-sell conversation rates.

• Program Execution Quality
 On-time, on-brief delivery of co-marketing programs - with the partner relationship strengthened as a result.

 Competencies and Behaviors:

• Influence Without Authority Operates effectively in an environment where the people you most depend on (partner counterparts, internal sales, product marketing) don't report into the same leadership. Builds alignment through credibility and relationships.

• Revenue-First Thinking Connects every program to pipeline and revenue. Doesn't measure success by content produced or events run. Asks "what did this produce?" and builds programs that are designed to answer that question.

• Partner-Facing Presence Comfortable representing 6sense externally. Shows up in partner conversations with enough confidence and preparation to be a genuine asset in the room.

• Execution Discipline Manages the complexity of co-marketing at pace. Gets joint programs across the finish line even when approval chains are complex.

• Cross-Functional Orchestration Works fluidly across product marketing, demand generation, content, field marketing, and BD to bring partner programs to life.

 Educational and Experience Requirements:

• 5 or more years in B2B marketing, with at least 2 years in a field marketing role, partner marketing, alliance marketing, or ecosystem marketing role where you owned outcomes and field programs.

• Experience working directly with external partner stakeholders. You have presented to partner leadership, negotiated co-marketing agreements, and maintained productive relationships through disagreements.

• A clear point of view on how to measure partner marketing impact, including how to handle the attribution ambiguity that comes with the territory.

• Familiarity with the B2B SaaS technology ecosystem: how ISV partnerships, technology integrations, and co-sell motions work in practice.

 Base Salary Range: $83,317.50 - $122,199.00. The base salary range represents the anticipated low and high end of the base salary range for this position. Actual salaries may vary and may be above or below the range based on various factors, including but not limited to work location and experience. The base salary is one component of 6sense’s total compensation package for this position. Other compensation may include a bonus program or commission plan, and stock options if approved by 6sense’s board. title: Dealer Development Manager (Nashville, TN)
description:
Headquarters: United States (Remote)

 Upgrade helps customers move in the right direction with affordable and responsible financial products. Since 2017, we’ve helped over 7.5 million customers access over $42 billion in consumer credit. With a relentless focus on improving our customers' financial well-being, we build products that put more money in their pocket and support their journey toward a better financial future. We’re backed by some of the most prominent technology investors and were most recently valued at $7.3B.

 We’re consistently recognized for our collaborative and inclusive culture. Most recently, we were named one of the World’s Top Fintech Companies by CNBC, Best Places to Work by Built In, Best Places to Work by the San Francisco Business Times, America’s Greatest Workplaces by Newsweek, Best Startup Employer by Forbes, and Healthiest Employers by Phoenix Business Journal.

 We’re looking for new team members who get excited about designing and delivering new and better products. Come join us and help build a better financial future for millions of people.

 About the Role:

 The Dealer Development Manager will represent Upgrade Inc (Auto Finance Division) and promote our indirect lending programs. They will develop, maintain, and grow business partnerships between Upgrade Inc. and our dealership partners. The Dealer Development Manager is also responsible for staying up-to-date on local market conditions and industry trends. In this role, you will work with internal partners to find solutions that better serve our customers, and build long lasting relationships with key decision makers to drive growth and continuous improvement.

 This position requires residency in the Greater Nashville Area.

 What You’ll Do:

 Dealer Relationship Management

• Develop and maintain relationships with new and existing dealer partners

• Act as a trusted advisor to dealership owners, GMs, and F&I managers

• Conduct regular in-person dealership visits based on a structured drive schedule

• Deliver consistent follow-up and service to ensure dealer satisfaction and loyalty

 Dealer Acquisition & Activation

• Identify, onboard, and activate new dealer partners

• Drive dealer sign-ups and first deals (“activation”)

• Re-engage inactive dealers (e.g., no deals in 90 days) and return them to production

• Execute onboarding training to ensure dealers understand programs and systems

 Production & Volume Growth

• Achieve monthly funding and application volume goals

• Increase contracts per active dealer and overall territory production

• Focus on growing volume in Tier 3–5 segments while maintaining quality

• Drive penetration targets (e.g., 3+ and 5+ deals per dealer per month)

 Credit & Deal Structuring

• Partner closely with underwriting/credit teams to structure deals effectively

• Educate dealers on program guidelines, stips, and deal packaging

• Improve pull-through by coaching dealers on submitting clean, fundable deals

 Portfolio Performance & Quality

• Monitor dealer portfolio performance (delinquency, charge-offs, profitability)

• Manage dealer mix to align with company risk appetite and profitability goals

• Shift focus toward preferred collateral and higher-performing dealers

• Ensure adherence to compliance, credit policies, and documentation standards

 Training & Dealer Development

• Conduct ongoing product and process training with dealership staff

• Educate dealers on value-added products

• Provide market insights and best practices to improve dealer success

• Position the company as a relationship-driven partner vs. transactional lender

 Territory & Activity Management

• Maintain a disciplined weekly drive schedule maximizing in-person dealer time

• Track and manage activity through CRM (e.g., Salesforce)

• Analyze territory performance and adjust strategy based on data

• Participate in team calls, sales meetings, and performance reviews

 What We Look For:

• 2+ years of experience in indirect auto finance, auto sales, or related field

• Strong understanding of credit tiers, loan structuring, and dealership operations

• Proven ability to build relationships and drive sales growth

• Excellent communication, negotiation, and problem-solving skills

• Self-motivated with strong time management and territory planning skills

• Ability to travel locally (significant field time required)

 What We Offer You:

• Competitive salary, uncapped commission and stock option plan

• Paid coverage of medical, dental and vision insurance

• Flexible PTO

• Competitive 401(k) and RRSP program

• Opportunities for professional growth and development

• Paid parental leave

• Health & wellness initiatives

 #LI-Hybrid

 Environmental & Working Conditions

 Work is performed indoors in a fast-paced environment that requires the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet established workflows, schedules, and service expectations.

 Employees regularly input, retrieve, and exchange information accurately using digital systems and applications to support operational and customer service objectives.

 The role requires the ability to receive and exchange information with customers, peers, supervisors, and cross-functional partners through available communication channels, which may include meetings, email, phone, and digital collaboration tools, and may involve real-time, verbal, or in-person exchanges depending on business need.

 Job duties may involve managing a high volume of inbound and/or outbound customer interactions and work activities using telecommunications and computer systems. The role requires the ability to read, analyze, and interpret information displayed on computer screens and remain in a working posture for extended periods, consistent with the demands of the position.

 Work may be performed in a contact center, office, or remote environment, depending on business needs and the nature of the role. Onsite work environments may include shared workspaces, standard office lighting, and moderate background noise typical of customer service or operational settings.

Agencies must obtain advance written approval from Upgrade's Talent Acquisition department to submit resumes and only in conjunction with a valid, fully executed agreement.

title: Manager, Customer Success - Upmarket
description:
Headquarters: United States, Remote

 Our Mission:

 6sense's mission is to multiply what matters: growth, retention, and efficiency. We envision a future where companies, teams and people reach their full potential.

 Our People:

 People are the heart and soul of 6sense. We serve with passion and purpose. We live by our Being 6sense values of Win as One Team, Stay Curious, Do The Right Thing, Own the Outcome, and Create Belonging. Every 6sensor plays a part in deﬁning the future of our industry-leading technology. 6sense is a place where difference-makers roll up their sleeves, take risks, act with integrity, and measure success by the value we create for our customers. We want 6sense to be the best chapter of your career.

 The Role

 As a Manager, Customer Success, you will lead a team of approximately 7-8 Customer Success Managers responsible for a combined portfolio of Upmarket customers with annual contract values ranging from $100K to $500K and representing approximately $15M-$20M in ARR.

 You will be responsible for driving customer retention, adoption, customer value realization, and operational excellence across your team's portfolio while developing and coaching a high-performing team of Customer Success Managers. This role requires a strong people leader who can balance business performance, talent development, forecasting discipline, and customer outcomes.

 Success in this role requires the ability to develop top talent, create accountability, establish operational rigor, and partner cross-functionally to ensure customers realize measurable business value from their investment in 6sense.

 You will work closely with Sales, Professional Services, Support, Product, Marketing, and Revenue Operations to help customers achieve their goals while contributing to the continued growth and scale of the Customer Success organization.

 What You'll Do

 Lead and Develop a High-Performing Team

• Lead, coach, and develop a team of approximately 7-8 Customer Success Managers supporting Upmarket customers.

• Create a culture of accountability, customer-centricity, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

• Conduct regular coaching sessions, performance reviews, talent assessments, and career development conversations.

• Establish clear expectations and operating rhythms that drive consistent execution and customer outcomes.

• Recruit, onboard, and develop Customer Success talent while supporting succession planning across the organization.

• Inspire and motivate a team that consistently delivers exceptional customer experiences and business results.

 Drive Customer Success Outcomes

• Lead a team responsible for customers with annual contract values between $100K and $500K and a combined portfolio of approximately $15M-$20M in ARR.

• Drive strong Gross Revenue Retention (GRR), customer adoption, customer satisfaction, and value realization across the portfolio.

• Coach Customer Success Managers on account strategy, executive stakeholder engagement, success planning, renewal strategy, risk mitigation, and value delivery, ensuring they understand and own the renewal process.

• Ensure Customer Success Managers proactively identify customer risks and execute strategies to improve retention outcomes.

• Partner with Sales leadership to align on customer health, growth opportunities, and strategic account planning.

• Drive a high level of customer engagement and executive alignment across key accounts.

 Drive Operational Excellence

• Own portfolio forecasting processes, renewal inspections, customer health reviews, and risk management practices.

• Ensure consistent execution of success plans, Executive Business Reviews (EBRs), account reviews, and customer engagement standards.

• Use data and analytics to identify trends, improve performance, and drive informed decision-making.

• Drive adoption of Customer Success processes, tools, and best practices across the team.

• Champion initiatives that improve efficiency, scalability, forecast accuracy, and customer outcomes.

 Partner Across the Business

• Collaborate closely with Sales, Product, Professional Services, Support, Marketing, and RevOps to deliver a world-class customer experience.

• Act as a voice of the customer and advocate for customer needs across the organization.

• Support strategic initiatives focused on customer retention, product adoption, operational scale, and customer value realization.

• Help shape the future of Customer Success programs, processes, and operating models as the business continues to grow.

 What We're Looking For

 We’re looking for new team members who get excited about designing and delivering new and better products. Come join us and help build a better financial future for millions of people.

 About the Role:

 The Dealer Development Manager will represent Upgrade Inc (Auto Finance Division) and promote our indirect lending programs. They will develop, maintain, and grow business partnerships between Upgrade Inc. and our dealership partners. The Dealer Development Manager is also responsible for staying up-to-date on local market conditions and industry trends. In this role, you will work with internal partners to find solutions that better serve our customers, and build long lasting relationships with key decision makers to drive growth and continuous improvement. This position requires residency in Dallas/Fort Worth, TX.

 What You’ll Do:

 Dealer Relationship Management

• Develop and maintain relationships with new and existing dealer partners

• Act as a trusted advisor to dealership owners, GMs, and F&I managers

• Deliver consistent follow-up and service to ensure dealer satisfaction and loyalty

• Re-engage inactive dealers (e.g., no deals in 90 days) and return them to production

 Production & Volume Growth

• Partner closely with underwriting/credit teams to structure deals effectively

• Improve pull-through by coaching dealers on submitting clean, fundable deals

 Portfolio Performance & Quality

• Monitor dealer portfolio performance (delinquency, charge-offs, profitability)

• Manage dealer mix to align with company risk appetite and profitability goals

• Shift focus toward preferred collateral and higher-performing dealers

• Ensure adherence to compliance, credit policies, and documentation standards

 Training & Dealer Development

• Conduct ongoing product and process training with dealership staff

• Educate dealers on value-added products

• Provide market insights and best practices to improve dealer success

• Position the company as a relationship-driven partner vs. transactional lender

 Territory & Activity Management

• Maintain a disciplined weekly drive schedule maximizing in-person dealer time

• Track and manage activity through CRM (e.g., Salesforce)

• Analyze territory performance and adjust strategy based on data

• Participate in team calls, sales meetings, and performance reviews

• 2+ years of experience in indirect auto finance, auto sales, or related field

• Strong understanding of credit tiers, loan structuring, and dealership operations

• Proven ability to build relationships and drive sales growth

• Excellent communication, negotiation, and problem-solving skills

• Self-motivated with strong time management and territory planning skills

• Paid coverage of medical, dental and vision insurance

• Flexible PTO

• Opportunities for professional growth and development

title: Sr. Software Engineer, Cloud Platform
description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

As a Senior Engineer in the Infrastructure org, you will help evolve the cloud foundations behind every Samsara product. Your goal will be to reduce systemic production risk and enable continued growth by making infrastructure safer to change, easier to operate, and more resilient and cost-efficient at scale.

You will bring deep expertise in at least one infrastructure domain, such as compute and workload orchestration, networking, storage and stateful systems, or cloud control planes, and apply it across our multi-account, multi-region AWS environment. You will lead work such as modernizing compute and stateful infrastructure, strengthening capacity and failure isolation, and building standardized infrastructure-as-code workflows and reusable automation.

You will partner with product engineering teams to turn recurring risks and manual operations into durable platforms and paved paths. We do not expect you to be an expert in every infrastructure domain. We are looking for engineers who have built and operated critical systems at significant scale, understand how infrastructure fails, and can use that experience to improve both our platforms and our engineering practices.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: The software, firmware, and hardware you build will result in real-world impact, helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are a life-long learner: We have ambitious goals. Every Samsarian has a growth mindset as we work with a wide range of technologies, challenges, and customers that push us to learn on the go.
  • You believe customers are more than a number: Samsara engineers enjoy a rare closeness to the end user and you will have the opportunity to participate in customer interviews, collaborate with customer success and product managers, and use metrics to ensure our work is translating into better customer outcomes.
  • You are a team player: Working on our Samsara Engineering teams requires a mix of independent effort and collaboration. Motivated by our mission, we’re all racing toward our connected operations vision, and we intend to win together.

In this role, you will:

  • Design, build, and operate reliable cloud platforms, bringing depth in one or more areas such as compute, networking, storage, stateful systems, or infrastructure control planes.
  • Improve the scalability, capacity management, isolation, recovery, and cost efficiency of critical production infrastructure.
  • Build standardized infrastructure-as-code workflows and reusable automation that support self-service provisioning, testing, progressive rollout, reconciliation, rollback, and drift prevention.
  • Identify shared failure modes and build safeguards that prevent localized failures from escalating into broad customer impact.
  • Contribute to multi-account, multi-region, and isolated AWS architectures, including regulated environments such as GovCloud.
  • Participate in operational ownership and incident response, using incidents and near misses to drive durable architectural improvements.
  • Mentor engineers, raise the quality of infrastructure design and operational judgment, and establish patterns that can be adopted across the organization.
  • Clearly communicate architecture, trade-offs, risks, and migration plans to technical and organizational stakeholders.
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

Minimum requirements for this role.

  • 6+ years of experience designing and building software, infrastructure, or distributed systems, including operating critical systems in production.
  • Deep expertise in at least one of the following: compute and workload orchestration, networking, storage and stateful systems, or cloud infrastructure control planes.
  • Strong software-engineering fundamentals in Go, Python, Java, or a similar language.
  • Hands-on experience designing and operating infrastructure on a major public cloud platform; AWS experience is preferred.
  • Experience using infrastructure as code, such as Terraform, to safely manage production infrastructure.
  • Strong understanding of capacity management, failure domains, observability, rollout safety, and production recovery.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical initiatives across teams and through ambiguous problem spaces.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Designing and operating large-scale compute or container platforms such as ECS, EKS, Kubernetes, or similar orchestration systems.
  • Designing and operating stateful distributed systems such as Kafka, OpenSearch, managed databases, caching, or large-scale storage platforms.
  • Building internal infrastructure platforms, control planes, or self-service developer experiences adopted across multiple teams.
  • Designing multi-account or multi-region cloud architectures with strong workload isolation and disaster recovery.
  • Leading major infrastructure migrations while maintaining availability and controlling operational risk.
  • Delivering measurable improvements in infrastructure capacity, cost efficiency, or developer self-service.

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email accessibleinterviewing@samsara.com or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.
